statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH (yellow). The 1.63% gap-down open has not only been retraced, it has been exceeded: the Nasdaq-100 cash index trades 29,256.92, down 0.38%, and has just printed a new session high of 29,257.57 against a 28,867.67 low. That extension is the one genuine one-way element in the tape, and it lifts Tail three points to 21 and back into the watch band. Every cross-asset amplifier continues to decay: VIX 16.72 off an 18.17 high, the 10-year 4.953% after tagging 5.012%, WTI $101.55 and Brent $105.83 off peaks near $104.79 and $109.44. Stress eases a point to 72.
recommendation: Tail at 21 sits in the watch band, so the mapped state is WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. The danger window is unchanged at 19:00-20:00 UTC, covering the final cash hour, where conditional Tail peaks at 23, two points below the block mapping. The conditional path returns to the low band across the post-close, overnight and Asian sessions, re-enters the watch band from Tuesday's European morning, and reaches 23 again for the 13:30 UTC cash open. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Gap more than fully retraced: NDX prints a new session high at 29,257.57 while VIX, the 10-year and crude all hold off their extremes; Tail rises to 21 and re-enters the watch band, with 19:00-20:00 UTC retained as the danger window
body:
The absorption of the opening gap is now complete and has carried past its own starting point. As of the 17:29 UTC quote the Nasdaq-100 cash index is at 29,256.92, down 111.52 points or 0.38% against a 29,368.44 previous close, having opened at 28,890.93 on a 1.63% gap. The session range is 28,867.67 to 29,257.57, which places the index within a point of its session high, and that high is a new one: an hour ago the session peak stood at 29,208.57. The index has recovered roughly 389 points, or 1.35%, from a low set within minutes of the cash open and untouched for about four hours since.

That last fact is the reason this assessment moves rather than holds. A completed retracement of a gap is the structural opposite of a pathological path and was scored as such in the previous hour. A retracement that keeps extending into new session highs is a different object: it is a sustained directional leg, and a leg that runs for four hours without giving back a meaningful portion of itself is the specific structure that denies a reverse or grid approach the mean reversion it depends on. Tail therefore rises three points to 21 and returns to the watch band. It is held well below the block mapping because that structure is currently the only amplifier present, and because the distance remaining to the previous close is only 0.38%, which places a natural supply reference immediately overhead.

Everything else in the cross-asset picture continues to stabilise rather than amplify. VIX is quoted at 16.72, still up 5.56% against a 15.84 close, but it has traded down from an 18.17 session high to sit near its session low of 16.58. The 10-year Treasury yield printed 5.012% earlier today, its first touch of 5% since 2023, and has since fallen to 4.953%, below its 4.975% previous close and near the low end of a 4.934% to 5.012% range; the Federal Reserve H.15 release puts the 2-year at 4.56% and the 10-year at 4.95% for 10 September, so the curve move is contained rather than a broad repricing. Crude has done the same: Brent reached about $109.44 and WTI about $104.79 during the European afternoon and are now quoted at $105.83 and $101.55. An amplifier that fails to extend after making its high is not contributing to the probability of a no-retracement path, and an index grinding higher while implied volatility falls to session lows is describing a low-realised-volatility drift rather than a violent impulse.

The catalyst stack is unchanged and verified from current reporting. Reuters reports that calls from the heads of Anthropic, OpenAI and xAI for a slower pace of AI model development drove a selloff in semiconductors, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down about 5.7%, Nvidia off roughly 3% and Intel, AMD and Marvell down 5%, 5% and 6%. The Motley Fool reports the same session with Micron down about 5.6% and SK Hynix about 7.4%, while Microsoft gained 1.9% and Alphabet 2% on the view that hardware spending restraint favours software. Euronews reports that Saudi Arabia shut its East-West pipeline after drone attacks, that a merchant vessel was struck in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, and that flows through the strait have fallen from about 20 million barrels a day before the war to roughly 7 million.

That dispersion is the single most important reason the index is not trending in the conventional sense, and it is why the dominant mode is published as mixed rather than as a directional label. A market in which one industry is down close to 6% while another is up 3% is distributing risk internally rather than compressing it into one direction, and the index-level advance is the arithmetic of that rotation rather than a broad bid. Consistent with the published risk definitions, that conflict raises Stress and disciplines Confidence rather than forcing Tail higher. The shared cross-asset context file was checked and found stale and partial: it was collected at 14:26 UTC, roughly three hours before this assessment and beyond the 90-minute freshness limit set by the inherited contract, and its calendar section was unavailable. It was therefore not used as supporting evidence, and all price levels, catalysts and the seven-day event list were verified independently from primary and reputable current sources.

The remaining live risks are event risks rather than path risks. The pipeline outage is physical and unrepaired, so a fresh Gulf headline can reprice crude in any hour, including the thin overnight session. The FOMC decision and Summary of Economic Projections arrive at 18:00 UTC on Wednesday with the press conference at 18:30 UTC, and US Retail Sales lands at 12:30 UTC the same morning, which keeps the bond market as the dominant cross-asset channel into midweek and typically compresses realised volatility on the eve of the meeting. Stress eases one point to 72, still firmly in the high band, and Confidence holds at 89: price, volatility, rates, energy, catalyst and calendar evidence is current and verified.

The danger window stays at 19:00 to 20:00 UTC, the final cash hour, unchanged from the previous assessment. It is the point at which a day that has more than recovered its gap either confirms into the settlement or gives the advance back, and the moment at which a late crude headline would meet the thinnest liquidity of the cash session. Conditional Tail peaks at 23 there, two points below the block mapping, reflecting a scheduled transition and the single live path amplifier rather than any observed closing structure. Beyond it the conditional path returns to the low band overnight, re-enters the watch band from Tuesday's European morning, and reaches 23 again at the 13:30 UTC cash open.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the Claude series ran through the low band during Sunday's US evening, entered the watch band from 21:00 UTC as the AI-slowdown and Middle East supply stories developed, and reached the elevated band at 09:00 and 10:00 UTC when NQ set a sequence of lower lows under a trend-down mode. It stepped back to the watch band at 11:00 and 12:00 UTC, returned to the elevated band at 13:00 UTC when the first bounce faded into the cash open, then eased steadily through 14:00, 15:00 and 16:00 UTC as the gap was absorbed, reaching 18 and the low band in the hour before this assessment. Stress held in the high band throughout, between 72 and 79, and Confidence improved from 72 to 89 as live price evidence became available. All 24 hourly slots are available from published Claude history.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook is built on an opening gap that has now been more than fully retraced, with the index printing a new session high while VIX, the 10-year and crude all hold back from their session extremes. Conditional Tail holds at 21 through the remaining cash afternoon and peaks at 23 in the 19:00 UTC power hour that forms the published danger window. It then settles between 17 and 20 across the post-close, overnight and Asian sessions, with small uplifts where crude has typically repriced first on Middle East developments. The path re-enters the watch band from Tuesday's European morning, eases again into the pre-FOMC compression of the European afternoon, and peaks at 23 for the 13:30 UTC cash open, two points below the block mapping. Confidence declines steadily with distance from the last verified price observation. Every hour beyond the current one is conditional risk, not observed structure.
